response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ci.country, AVG(cs.wins) AS a FROM constructorStandings cs JOIN races r ON r.raceId=cs.raceId JOIN circuits ci ON ci.circuitId=r.circuitId GROUP BY ci.country), o AS (SELECT AVG(cs.wins) AS v FROM constructorStandings cs JOIN races r ON r.raceId=cs.raceId JOIN circuits ci ON ci.circuitId=r.circuitId), g AS (SELECT AVG(c.a) AS v FROM c, o WHERE c.a > o.v) SELECT AVG(c.a) AS mean_avg_wins, AVG(c.a - o.v) AS mean_excess_over_overall, AVG(c.a - g.v) AS mean_excess_over_group FROM c, o, g WHERE c.a > g.v

assumptions.assumption: Each country's average is the mean of constructorStandings.wins over all standings rows at races held at circuits in that country. The wins column is a season-to-date running count, but the request asks for the average of that column per standings entry, so it is used as is.
The 'overall average' is the pooled average of wins across all standings entries (each entry weighted equally), not the mean of the country averages.
The 'average of the above-average group' is the unweighted mean of those countries' averages.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-country averages, not the pooled row-level average.
